title: LAW N° 033/2026 OF 24/07/2026  GOVERNING THE NATIONAL BANK OF RWANDA

articles.heading: Purpose of this Law
Interpretation In this Law
articles.text:
(a) “regulations” means a written
instrument issued by the NBR in
accordance with its responsibilities,
and whose purpose is to specify, in
detail, procedures for the
implementation of the provisions of
this Law or any other law;
(b) “directives” means a written
instrument issued by the NBR that sets
out prescriptions or prohibitions and is
intended for a natural person or legal
entity;
(c) “reserve funds” means any liquid
assets set aside for future use to address
budgetary shortfalls in respect of
14
urgent expenditures and meet
unforeseen costs, and which are
ordinarily regarded as additional
assets;
(d) “Governor” means the Governor of
the NBR;
(e) “Deputy Governor” means the
Deputy Governor of the NBR;
(f) “financial institution” includes –
(i) a bank;
(ii) a deposit-taking microfinance
institution;
(iii) a non-deposit-taking lending
institution;
(iv) an insurance institution;
(v) a social security institution;
(vi)a mandatory or voluntary
pension scheme;
15
(vii) a forex bureau;
(viii) a payment services
provider;
(ix) a payment system operator;
and
(x) a financial institution that is
not supervised by another
institution under a specific
law.
(g) “legal entity” means any company,
cooperative or other entity, other than a
natural person, having rights and
obligations under the law;
(h) “guidelines” means a written
instrument issued by the NBR that
provides guidance in respect of
activities within the scope of its
responsibilities or powers;
(i) “agent of the NBR” means a financial
institution operating in Rwanda or
abroad that, pursuant to an agreement,
performs specific activities on behalf
16
of the NBR;
(j) “general policy” means administrative
policies, excluding monetary policy;
(k) “correspondent of the NBR” means a
financial institution operating abroad
with which the NBR enters into a
banking partnership agreement for the
purpose of holding accounts and
performing international financial
services on behalf of the NBR;
(l) “non-executive board member”
means a member of the Board of
Directors who is neither the Governor
nor the Deputy Governor;
(m)“trust and company service
provider” includes any person who –
(i) acts as a formation agent of a legal
person;
(ii) acts as, or arranges for another
person to act as, a director or
secretary of a company, a partner of
a partnership, or in a similar
17
capacity in relation to any other
legal entity;
(iii) provides a registered office,
business address, correspondence
or administrative address for a
company, a partnership or any
other legal person or legal
arrangement;
(iv)acts as, or arranges for another
person to act as, a trustee of an
express trust or, performs an
equivalent function for another
form of legal arrangement; or
(v) acts as, or arranges for another
person to act as, a nominee
shareholder for another person.
18

articles.heading: Capital (1) The capital of the NBR is FRW 7,000,000,000, wholly subscribed by the Government of Rwanda. It is not
articles.text:
subject to any lien or encumbrance.
(2) The capital of the NBR may be
increased either through the
capitalisation of reserve funds, upon
advice of the Board of Directors or
through additional contributions from
the State of Rwanda upon approval by
a Presidential Order.

articles.heading: Legal personality, independence and autonomy (1) The NBR has legal personality and enjoys independence, as well as
articles.text:
administrative and financial autonomy.
(2) In the exercise of their powers or in the
discharge of their responsibilities, the
NBR, its staff members, its agents and
the members of its decision-making
bodies are not subject to any external
interference from any person or organ.
19
(3) The NBR is neither subject to
registration in the commercial register,
nor to the rules governing public
accounting. However, the NBR
remains subject to the ordinary rules of
commercial accounting and is, in its
commercial relations with third
parties, governed by commercial
legislation unless specific legislation
governing it provides otherwise.

articles.heading: Head office, branches, correspondents and agents of the NBR (1) The head office of the NBR is located
articles.text:
in the City of Kigali. It may, where
necessary, be relocated to any other
location within the territory of
Rwanda, upon approval by an Order of
the Prime Minister.
(2) The NBR may establish a branch at any
location within the national territory,
upon approval by the Board of
Directors.
(3) The NBR may appoint an agent or
20
correspondent for the conduct of its
activities.
CHAPTER II: MISSION,
RESPONSIBILITIES AND POWERS

articles.heading: Mission The mission of the NBR is to maintain price stability and a sound financial system, thereby
articles.text: enabling sustainable and inclusive growth.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the NBR The NBR has the following responsibilities
articles.text:
(a) to define and implement monetary
policy;
(b) to organise and supervise the foreign
exchange market;
(c) to supervise financial institutions;
(d) to supervise trust and company service
providers;
(e) to supervise and oversee payment
systems;
21
(f) to conduct financial stability
assessments to support sustainable
economic growth and development;
(g) to develop, formulate and implement
policies for the efficient clearing and
settlement of payment systems;
(h) to manage currency;
(i) to hold and manage official foreign
exchange reserves;
(j) to act as State Cashier;
(k) to collect, compile and disseminate
monetary and financial statistics;
(l) to monitor and promote the soundness
of financial institutions to ensure their
compliance with laws governing them;
(m)to establish policies for safeguarding
the rights and interests of customers,
depositors and other persons with any
interest other than making deposits in
financial institutions, having regard to
the need for financial institutions to
22
compete effectively in the market and
take all reasonable measures to prevent
risks;
(n) to provide opinions, on its own
initiative or at the request of the
Government, on the domestic financial
situation of the country and propose
appropriate measures. Opinions of the
NBR on the status of currency, access
to credit and the economy in general
are particularly sought in the event the
Government intends to take monetary
or financial measures;
(o) to undertake crisis management and
resolution, unless that mandate is
expressly assigned to another
institution under specific laws;
(p) to periodically communicate to the
public monetary and financial stability
strategies and the mechanisms for their
implementation;
23
(q) to discharge any other responsibility
related to or incidental to its functions
under this Law, or as may be provided
for by other laws.

articles.heading: Powers of the NBR The NBR has the following powers
articles.text:
(a) to issue regulations, directives or
guidelines;
(b) to grant, suspend and revoke licenses
or authorisations in relation to its
responsibilities;
(c) to impose administrative sanctions in
relation to its responsibilities;
(d) to establish a legal entity or acquire
shares in a domestic, foreign or
international company, where the
Board of Directors considers it
necessary, for the purposes of financial
sector innovation, the training of its
staff members or regulated institutions
and the welfare of its staff;
24
(e) to take decisions on matters within the
scope of its responsibilities as provided
for under this Law and other specific
laws.
CHAPTER III: ORGANISATION
Section One: Governing organs

articles.heading: Governing organs of the NBR The governing organs of the NBR are – (a) The Board of Directors; and
articles.text:
(b) The Management.
Subsection One: Board of Directors

articles.heading: Composition of the Board of Directors, appointment and term of office of its members (1) The Board of Directors consists of the
articles.text:
following 11 members:
(a) the Governor;
25
(b) the Deputy Governor;
(c) nine other members appointed and
removed by a Presidential Order,
selected on the basis of their
competence and expertise in the
fields of monetary, financial,
economic, accounting, risk
management, legal, information
technology or other disciplines
relevant to the functions of the
NBR.
(2) Not more than 30% of the members of
the Board of Directors may be civil
servants, with the Governor, the
Deputy Governor and a member of the
Board of Directors appointed from
academia or research institutions
excluded from the calculation of that
limit.
(3) The Governor serves as the
Chairperson of the Board of Directors
and is assisted by the Deputy
Governor, unless otherwise provided
by their appointing authority.
(4) Members of the Board of Directors,
other than the Governor and the
26
Deputy Governor, serve a four-year
term, renewable once.
(5) Members of the Board of Directors are
appointed on a staggered basis so as to
ensure the continuity of the
administration of the NBR.

articles.heading: Requirements for being a member of the Board of Directors For a person to be a member of the Board of
articles.text:
Directors must –
(a) be a person of integrity;
(b) not have been definitively sentenced to
imprisonment for a term equal to or
more than 6 months;
(c) not have been convicted of the crime of
genocide ideology and related
offences; and
(d) not have been convicted of the crime of
genocide.
27

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Board of Directors (1) The Board of Directors formulates the general policy of the NBR and
articles.text:
oversees its implementation.
(2) In particular, the Board of Directors
has the following responsibilities:
(a) to formulate policies relating to the
discharge of the functions of the
NBR and define its organisational
chart;
(b) to deliberate on and authorize the
minting, issuance or withdrawal of
banknotes, coins or any other form
of currency and their features, and
submit them to the competent
authority for approval;
(c) to determine the terms and
conditions of service of the
Governor and the Deputy
Governor, that are not provided for
under this Law;
28
(d) to approve the annual action plan
and budget of the NBR and any
modifications thereto, where
necessary;
(e) to appoint an independent auditor
for the NBR;
(f) to approve the financial statements
prepared by an independent auditor
and decide on the distribution of
operating income;
(g) to approve the annual activity
report that the Governor submits to
the President of the Republic and
Parliament;
(h) to develop and adopt the Charter of
the Board of Directors and other
rules regulating the discharge of its
functions;
(i) to advise on increasing the capital
of the NBR through the
capitalisation of reserve funds,
where necessary.
29

articles.heading: Powers of the Board of Directors (1) The Board of Directors has the following powers
articles.text:
(a) to supervise the implementation of the
general policy and the management of
the NBR;
(b) to adopt regulations and directives;
(c) to make a decision relating to the
supervision of financial institutions in
accordance with laws;
(d) to adopt the internal rules and policies
of the NBR;
(e) to adopt staff rules governing the
recruitment, appointment,
management, and dismissal of the staff
members of the NBR, and their salaries
and other fringe benefits;
(f) to adopt specific rules that regulate
procurement activities of the NBR;
30
(g) to adopt the internal audit charter in
compliance with international
standards;
(h) to establish branches of the NBR and
determine their locations;
(i) to establish Committees of the Board
of Directors. However, the Governor
or the Deputy Governor is not eligible
for membership on any Committee of
the Board of Directors;
(j) to determine the salaries and fringe
benefits of the Governor and the
Deputy Governor during and after their
terms of office, after consultation with
their appointing authority;
(k) to appoint members of special
committees who are not staff members
of the NBR and determine their fringe
benefits;
(l) to decide on the receipt, donation and
sale of property of the NBR and on the
31
use of its core capital;
(m)to decide on any other matter relating
to the mission of the NBR that is not
entrusted by this Law or any other law
to any other organ of the NBR.
(2) Except for its powers to supervise the
implementation of the general policy
and the management of the NBR, the
Board of Directors may delegate some
of its powers to the Governor,
including, in particular, the power to
issue regulations or directives and
make the decisions provided for under
Paragraph (1)(c).

articles.heading: Duties of the Chairperson of the Board of Directors The Chairperson of the Board of Directors has
articles.text:
the following duties:
(a) to convene and preside over the
meeting of the Board of Directors and
coordinate its activities;
(b) to monitor the implementation of
resolutions of the Board of Directors;
32
(c) to perform any other duty relating to
the responsibilities of the Board of
Directors as may be assigned by the
Board of Directors.

articles.heading: Duties of the Deputy Chairperson of the Board of Directors The Deputy Chairperson of the Board of
articles.text:
Directors has the following duties:
(a) to assist the Chairperson of the Board
of Directors and deputize for him or
her during his or her absence;
(b) to perform any other duty relating to
the responsibilities of the Board of
Directors as may be assigned by the
Board of Directors.

articles.heading: Incompatibilities with membership of the Board of Directors (1) The duties of members of the Board of
articles.text:
Directors of the NBR are incompatible
with membership of Parliament or of
the Cabinet, and with any form of
participation, whether remunerated or
not, in an institution subject to the
33
supervision of the NBR.
(2) No member of the Board of Directors,
other than the Governor and the
Deputy Governor, may be a staff
member of the NBR.
(3) A member of the Board of Directors,
whether acting individually or through
a company in which he or she holds
shares, is not allowed to bid for tenders
of the NBR.

articles.heading: Convening and holding the meeting of the Board of Directors (1) The Board of Directors holds its
articles.text:
ordinary meeting once every quarter.
The meeting is convened and presided
over by the Chairperson of the Board
of Directors or, in his or her absence,
by the Deputy Chairperson.
(2) The notice convening a meeting of the
Board of Directors is submitted in
writing to the members of the Board of
34
Directors at least ten working days
before the meeting is held.
(3) The Board of Directors may hold an
extraordinary meeting at the request of
its Chairperson or of two thirds of its
members. The meeting considers only
the items included on the agenda.
(4) The quorum for a meeting of the Board
of Directors consists of two thirds of its
members. However, where a second
meeting of the Board of Directors is
convened following an inquorate
meeting, such a meeting takes place if
at least one half of its members are
present.

articles.heading: Invitation of a resource person to a meeting of the Board of Directors (1) The Board of Directors may invite to
articles.text:
its meeting any other person whom it
considers capable of providing it with
advice on any item on its agenda.
35
(2) Any person so invited is neither
allowed to vote nor to follow
deliberations on other items on the
agenda.
(3) The person invited to a meeting of the
Board of Directors must maintain the
confidentiality of matters that come to
his or her knowledge in the course of
the meeting.

articles.heading: Decision-making and minutes of the meeting of the Board of Directors (1) The Board of Directors takes decisions
articles.text:
by consensus. Failing consensus,
decisions are taken by a majority of the
votes cast by the members present at
the meeting. In the event of a tied vote,
the chair of the meeting has a casting
vote.
(2) The minutes of a meeting of the Board
of Directors are signed by all members
present at the meeting.
(3) A copy of the decisions of the meeting
of the Board of Directors is transmitted
to the Minister in charge of finance
36
immediately upon the conclusion of
the meeting.
(4) Without prejudice to the provisions of
this Law, the Charter of the Board of
Directors determines the manner in
which the minutes thereof are drawn
up and other matters pertaining to the
conduct of its meetings.

articles.heading: Personal interest in an item under consideration (1) Where a member of the Board of Directors has a direct or indirect
articles.text:
personal interest in an item under
consideration, he or she immediately
discloses the nature of such an interest
to the Board of Directors.
(2) A member of the Board of Directors
having a personal interest in an item
under consideration does not attend the
meeting deliberating on the item.
37

articles.heading: Sitting allowances and other benefits accorded to a member of the Board of Directors attending a meeting
articles.text:
A Presidential Order determines sitting
allowances and other benefits accorded to a
member of the Board of Directors attending its
meeting, and such allowances and benefits
may not be reduced during the member’s term
of office.

articles.heading: Grounds for loss of membership of a member of the Board of Directors and procedures for his or her replacement
articles.text:
(1) A member of the Board of Directors
loses membership where –
(a) his or her term of office expires;
(b) he or she no longer fulfils the
requirements on the basis of which
he or she was appointed in that
capacity;
(c) he or she becomes incapable of
performing his or her duties by
reason of physical or mental
38
disability certified by an authorised
medical doctor;
(d) he or she resigns;
(e) he or she is dismissed; or
(f) he or she dies.
(2) Where the term of office of a member
of the Board of Directors is about to
expire, the Chairperson of the Board of
Directors notifies the appointing
authority thereof in writing at least 90
days prior to such expiry. If a member
of the Board of Directors ceases to hold
membership on any of the grounds
provided for under Paragraph (1)(c)
and (f), the Chairperson of the Board
of Directors gives notice to that effect
within seven days from the date he or
she becomes aware of such ground.
(3) If a member of the Board of Directors
ceases to hold membership, the
competent authority appoints a
replacement within 90 days from the
cessation of such membership.
39

articles.heading: Audit Committee of the Board of Directors (1) The Committees established by the Board of Directors that are provided
articles.text:
for under Article 13(1)(i) include an
Audit Committee of the Board of
Directors.
(2) The Audit Committee of the Board of
Directors operates in accordance with
its Charter.
(3) Non-executive members of the Board
of Directors who are civil servants may
serve on the Audit Committee of the
Board of Directors in an advisory
capacity only. However, civil servants
who are members of the Audit
Committee of the Board of Directors
and who are from academia or research
institutions have voting rights.
40
Subsection 2: Management

articles.heading: Composition of the Management, appointment and removal of its members (1) The Management of the NBR consists
articles.text:
of the Governor and the Deputy
Governor, who are appointed and
removed by a Presidential Order.
(2) The Governor and the Deputy
Governor are appointed within 90 days
from the date of occurrence of a
vacancy in the respective office, and
such appointment is subject to the
approval of the Senate.

articles.heading: Term of office of members of the Management
Duties of the Governor (1) The Governor has the following duties
articles.text:
(a) to serve as the legal representative
of the NBR;
41
(b) to lead and coordinate the activities
of the NBR;
(c) to sign any agreement concluded
by the NBR, annual reports,
statements of financial position,
statements of comprehensive
income and other financial
statements, correspondence, and
other documents of the NBR;
(d) to sign banknotes;
(e) to determine requirements for each
job position within the NBR;
(f) to recruit, appoint, manage and
remove staff members of the NBR
under the terms and conditions laid
down by the staff rules of the NBR;
(g) to establish operating procedures,
instructions, and service orders that
he or she considers necessary for
the proper management of the
NBR;
42
(h) to establish guidelines;
(i) to manage and implement the
approved budget of the NBR;
(j) to approve the agent or the
correspondent of the NBR;
(k) to submit to the Board of Directors
the action plan and draft budget for
every year;
(l) to perform any other duty relating
to the responsibilities of the NBR
as may be assigned by the Board of
Directors.
(2) Any other staff member of the NBR
may, except for the duty of signing
banknotes, perform the duties provided
for under this Article where so
empowered by the Governor.
(3) The Governor may cooperate with the
entities vested with supervisory
responsibilities over public organs in
performing the duties provided for
under Paragraph (1)(f).
43

articles.heading: Duties of the Deputy Governor The Deputy Governor has the following duties
Incompatibilities with the offices of Governor and Deputy Governor The offices of Governor and Deputy Governor
articles.text:
are incompatible with the holding of any other
full-time office.
44

articles.heading: Debt agreements that the Governor and the Deputy Governor are not allowed to sign The Governor and Deputy Governor are not
articles.text:
allowed to sign agreements that may be used
as collateral for refinancing by the NBR.

articles.heading: Grounds for cessation of office of Governor or Deputy Governor The Governor or Deputy Governor ceases to
articles.text:
hold such office where –
(a) his or her term of office expires;
(b) he or she no longer fulfils the
requirements on the basis of which he
or she was appointed in such office;
(c) he or she becomes incapable of
performing his or her duties by reason
of physical or mental disability
certified by an authorised medical
doctor;
(d) he or she resigns;
(e) he or she is dismissed; or
45
(f) he or she dies.
Section 2: Special Committees
Subsection One: Monetary Policy
Committee

articles.heading: Composition of the Monetary Policy Committee, appointment and term of office of its members
articles.text:
(1) The Monetary Policy Committee
consists of the following nine
members:
(a) the Governor, who also serves as
its Chairperson;
(b) the Deputy Governor, who also
serves as its Deputy Chairperson;
(c) two senior staff members of the
NBR appointed by the Governor,
including –
(i) one staff member with senior
management duties in terms of
monetary policy analysis; and
46
(ii) one staff member with senior
management duties in terms of
monetary policy operations.
(d) such other staff members of the
NBR as appointed by the
Governor;
(e) such other persons, not being staff
members of the NBR, as appointed
by the Board of Directors on the
basis of their knowledge,
experience and expertise relevant
to the responsibilities of the
Monetary Policy Committee.
(2) Members of the Monetary Policy
Committee appointed by the Board of
Directors who are referred to in
Paragraph (1)(e) serve for a term of
four years, renewable once.

articles.heading: Responsibility of the Monetary Policy Committee The Monetary Policy Committee is responsible for the formulation of the
articles.text:
monetary policy within the NBR.
47

articles.heading: Meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee, decision-making and minutes taking procedures (1) The Monetary Policy Committee
articles.text:
meets once every quarter and
whenever necessary. The meeting
convened and presided over by the
Chairperson or, in his or her absence,
by the Deputy Chairperson.
(2) The quorum for the meeting of the
Monetary Policy Committee consists
of two thirds of its members.
(3) The Monetary Policy Committee takes
its decisions by consensus. Failing
consensus, decisions are taken by a
majority of the votes cast by the
members present at the meeting,
excluding non-executive members of
the Committee who are civil servants,
except those drawn from academia or
research institutions. In the event of a
tied vote, the chair of the meeting has
a casting vote.
(4) Without prejudice to the provisions of
this Law, the rules of the Monetary
48
Policy Committee determine the
manner in which its meeting minutes
are drawn up and other matters
pertaining to the conduct of its
meetings.

articles.heading: Communication of the gist of the monetary policy Following each meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee, the NBR communicates,
articles.text:
within a reasonable period, the gist of the
monetary policy to be implemented.
Subsection 2: Financial Stability
Committee

articles.heading: Composition of the Financial Stability Committee, appointment and term of office of its members
articles.text:
(1) The Financial Stability Committee
consists of the following 11 members:
(a) the Governor, who also serves as
its Chairperson;
(b) the Deputy Governor, who also
serves as its Deputy Chairperson;
49
(c) three senior staff members of the
NBR appointed by the Governor,
including –
(i) one staff member with senior
management duties in terms of
financial stability;
(ii) one staff member with senior
management duties in terms of
monetary policy analysis;
(iii) one staff member with senior
management duties in terms of
monetary policy operations;
(d) other staff members of the NBR
appointed by the Governor who
possess knowledge, experience and
expertise relevant to the
responsibilities of the Committee;
(e) such other persons, not being staff
members of the NBR, as are
50
appointed by the Board of
Directors on the basis of their
knowledge, experience and
expertise relevant to the
responsibilities of the Committee.
(2) Members of the Financial Stability
Committee appointed by the Board of
Directors referred to in Paragraph
(1)(e) serve for a term of four years,
renewable once.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Financial Stability Committee The Financial Stability Committee has the
articles.text:
following responsibilities:
(a) to regularly review and ensure the
soundness and stability of the financial
system;
(b) to promote the stability of the
Rwandan financial system by
analysing it within its environment on
a permanent basis;
(c) to identify, monitor and publish the
risks associated with the financial
system in order to take appropriate
measures to prevent, reduce and
51
mitigate such risks.

articles.heading: Meeting of the Financial Stability Committee, decision-making and minutes taking procedures
articles.text:
(1) The Financial Stability Committee
meets once every quarter and
whenever necessary. The meeting is
convened and presided over by its
Chairperson or, in his or her absence,
by the Deputy Chairperson.
(2) The quorum for the meeting of
Financial Stability Committee consists
of two thirds of its members.
(3) The Financial Stability Committee
takes its decisions by consensus among
the members present at the meeting.
Failing consensus, decisions are taken
by a majority of the votes cast by the
members present at the meeting,
excluding non-executive members of
the Committee who are civil servants,
unless they are those drawn from
academia or research institutions. In
the event of a tied vote, the chair of the
52
meeting has a casting vote.
(4) Without prejudice to the provisions of
this Law, the rules of the Financial
Stability Committee determine the
manner in which its meeting minutes
are drawn up and other matters
pertaining to the conduct of its
meetings.

articles.heading: Communication of the gist of the financial stability After each meeting of the Financial Stability
articles.text:
Committee, the NBR communicates, within a
reasonable period, the gist of the financial
stability.
CHAPTER IV: CURRENCY
MANAGEMENT
Section One: National currency
management

articles.heading: Currency constituting legal tender in the Republic of Rwanda (1) The monetary unit of the Republic of
articles.text:
Rwanda is the Rwandan franc
53
abbreviated as “FRW”, hereinafter
referred to as “the franc”.
(2) The currency is in the form of
banknotes, coins or any other form
approved by the currency-issuing
authority.
(3) A Presidential Order establishes
banknotes, coins or any other form of
currency with legal tender status in the
Republic of Rwanda and determines
their features.
(4) A banknote bears the signatures of the
Governor and the Deputy Governor.
(5) Banknotes, coins or any other form of
currency that are legal tender in the
Republic of Rwanda remain legal
tender until they are demonetised.
(6) Any monetary obligation or
transaction entered into in the Republic
of Rwanda is presumed to be expressed
and settled in the Rwandan franc,
unless otherwise provided for by other
54
laws.

articles.heading: Value of the franc The value of the franc in terms of foreign exchange is determined in accordance with the
articles.text:
monetary policy strategy set by the NBR.
However, where exceptional circumstances
are likely to cause excessive speculation
against the franc, the NBR fixes the exchange
rate of the franc for a specified period.

articles.heading: Management of the currency
Limitations on the exchange of banknotes and coins (1) The exchange of banknotes is not subject to any limitation
articles.text:
(2) For each type of coin, the exchange is
limited to 100 times its unitary face
value, unless the creditor agrees to
receive coins exceeding this amount.
However, coins are accepted, without
limitation, where tendered to the NBR,
the Public Treasury or to a deposittaking financial institution.
55

articles.heading: Demonetisation of banknotes, coins or any other form of currency and procedures for its publication
articles.text:
(1) The NBR advises on the
demonetisation of banknotes, coins or
any other form of currency having
legal tender status.
(2) A Presidential Order demonetises
banknotes, coins or any other form of
currency having legal tender status and
specifies the time from which such
banknotes, coins or other form of
currency cease to be legal tender.
(3) The demonetisation of banknotes,
coins or any other form of currency
having legal tender status is published
in at least two media with a large
audience in the country. However,
such publication may be disregarded
under exceptional circumstances.
56
(4) The publication referred to in
Paragraph (3) specifies conditions
under which exchange transactions of
banknotes, coins or other form of
currency that have ceased to be legal
tender have to take place. After the date
specified in the publication, the NBR
decides on banknotes, coins or other
form of currency presented for
exchange beyond that date.
Section 2: Foreign reserves management

articles.heading: Authorised transactions For the purposes of maintaining and managing foreign reserves, the NBR may –
articles.text:
(a) buy, sell, hold, lend, and borrow
foreign currency in any form;
(b) engage in transactions with foreign
commercial banks, eligible foreign
counterparties, and other financial
institutions or agencies;
57
(c) conduct transactions in gold, for its
own account or for the account of third
parties;
(d) buy, sell or hold monetary gold, bullion
or other precious metals;
(e) invest in foreign currency in any
eligible asset class, currency and sector
as determined by its investment policy
and guidelines;
(f) open any account and hold balances in
foreign currency with approved
partners, whether domestic or foreign;
and
(g) conduct trade finance transactions and
issue or accept guarantees
denominated in foreign currencies.
58

articles.heading: Foreign exchange market organisation The NBR is responsible for the organisation and management of the foreign exchange
articles.text:
market. It issues regulations and directives
governing the market and ensures their
enforcement.

articles.heading: Management of the effects of exchange rate fluctuations (1) Foreign exchange gain and loss resulting from exchange transactions
articles.text:
are recognised in the statement of
profit and loss of the NBR.
(2) Unrealised gains or losses arising from
a revaluation of reserve exchange
holdings or international commitments
recorded in the balance sheet of the
NBR, owing to changes in the foreign
exchange system or in the exchange
value of the franc, are recorded in a
special account entitled “Foreign
Exchange Revaluation Account”.
(3) The NBR accounts for the revaluation
gains or losses in line with
international financial reporting
59
standards.
Section 3: Money market

articles.heading: Organisation of money market (1) The NBR issues regulations and directives relating to the organisation
articles.text:
and functioning of the money market,
designates entities authorised to
intervene in the market and specifies
the instruments that may be traded
thereon.
(2) The NBR ensures the smooth
operation of the interbank market and
oversees interbank operations.

articles.heading: Interventions by the NBR in money market (1) The NBR may intervene in the money market for the purposes of lending and
articles.text:
borrowing or buying and selling liquid
assets which can be resold through
repurchase agreements of securities
sold, pledging government or private
securities or other negotiable
60
instruments.
(2) The transactions provided for under
Paragraph (1) must not be conducted
for the benefit of the Public Treasury or
a securities-issuing agency.
(3) For the purposes of monetary policy,
the NBR may purchase, hold and sell
securities issued by the Government or
its entities. However, those purchases
are not made for the purpose of
financing any deficit in the
Government budget, and are effected
in the secondary market at market
rates.
(4) The NBR may also purchase and sell
its own negotiable monetary securities.
CHAPTER V: RELATIONS BETWEEN
THE NBR AND THE STATE, OTHER
BODIES AND INSTITUTIONS
Section One: Relations with the State,
public and international bodies
61

articles.heading: Management of State accounts (1) The NBR performs transactions relating to the banking and withdrawal
articles.text:
of State funds, to the borrowing
operations of the State and the payment
of its debts. It maintains in its books,
free of charge, the current account of
the Public Treasury, in accordance with
an agreement concluded with the
Ministry in charge of finance.
(2) The NBR may, at the request of the
Minister in charge of finance, open
other State accounts governed by
special legal provisions.
(3) The credit balances on the accounts
provided for under this Article do not
bear interest.

articles.heading: Domestic government debt securities The NBR participates, on the account of the Government, in the issuance and distribution
articles.text:
of domestic government debt securities, in
accordance with an agreement concluded with
the Ministry in charge of finance.
62

articles.heading: Loans to the State (1) The NBR does not grant loans to the State, except by way of direct advances
articles.text:
to meet a shortfall between public
revenue and public expenditures in the
Public Treasury in order to ensure its
smooth operation. Such direct
advances may not exceed 11% of the
State current revenue collected during
the preceding financial year.
(2) The NBR levies on the debit referred
to in Paragraph (1) interests computed
at the daily average rate of the
interbank market.
(3) The State repays, in cash, the advances
loaned to it by the NBR within the
financial year in which they are
granted.

articles.heading: Management of current accounts of other institutions (1) The NBR may open and maintain current accounts for any public entity
articles.text:
or State organ, foreign central bank,
international organisation or
63
diplomatic mission accredited in
Rwanda.
(2) The accounts provided for under this
Article cannot post a debit balance, and
credit balances on those accounts do
not bear interest.

articles.heading: Role of the NBR in relations between the State and international financial organisations (1) The NBR assists the central
articles.text:
government in its relations with
international financial organisations
and may also represent it both in such
organisations and at international
conferences.
(2) The NBR, in collaboration with the
central government, takes part in the
negotiations of foreign loans to be
received or granted and may represent
the State in such negotiations.
(3) The NBR assists the State in the
negotiations of international payments,
foreign exchange and clearing
agreements and is responsible for their
implementation.
64

articles.heading: Cooperation agreements between the NBR and foreign institutions with similar mission The NBR may enter into cooperation
articles.text:
agreements with a foreign central bank,
foreign supervisory organs, foreign financial
sector regulators and international financial
institutions.
Section 2: Relations of the NBR with
financial institutions in Rwanda

articles.heading: Management of accounts of financial institutions NBR may, under the conditions it determines,
articles.text:
open and keep accounts for a financial
institution.

articles.heading: Clearing The NBR, in conjunction with an authorised financial institution, may – (a) organise a clearing house to facilitate
articles.text:
the clearing of payment and credit
instruments;
65
(b) issue directives concerning payment
and credit instruments provided for
under Subparagraph (a), their
processing, collection, payment and
retention and determining the
operation of other clearing houses that
the NBR may entrust with the task of
examining payments;
(c) establish, where it deems necessary, an
electronic system used for the
settlement of payments relating to
funds and securities, and take part in
such payments effected through other
means;
(d) issue regulations and directives
relating to the clearing and payment
system.

articles.heading: Required reserves (1) The NBR may require a financial institution to maintain a minimum cash
articles.text:
balance specified by the NBR, in
respect of the total deposits or
A
66
liabilities of the financial institution.
(2) The minimum cash balance referred to
in Paragraph (1) consists of the balance
held with the financial institution and
may also include banknotes and coins
held in the vaults of banks or a deposittaking financial institution.
(3) The NBR imposes on a financial
institution that fails to maintain the
minimum cash balances a penalty
charge at an interest rate determined by
the NBR.

articles.heading: Granting of loans to a financial institution (1) The NBR may grant loans or advances to a financial institution under its
articles.text:
supervision, solely for the purpose of
carrying out its functions relating to
monetary policy and financial stability.
(2) The loans and advances provided for
under Paragraph (1) must be secured
by adequate collateral approved by the
NBR.
67
(3) The NBR may also provide emergency
liquidity assistance against adequate
collateral and on a short-term basis
only to a solvent but temporarily
illiquid financial institution, and such
assistance is repayable at a higher
interest rate.
(4) Directives determine the duration,
interest rate, and other conditions for
the granting of loans, advances, and
emergency liquidity assistance.
Section 3: Confidentiality in the NBR
operations

articles.heading: Duty of confidentiality (1) A member of the Board of Directors, a staff member of the NBR, or any other
articles.text:
person who acquires confidential
information, whether in the course of,
or after the cessation of, his or her
duties at NBR or otherwise, is bound
by a duty of confidentiality.
68
(2) Non-compliance with the provisions of
Paragraph (1) is punishable under
relevant laws.
(3) The persons provided for under
Paragraph (1) do not incur punishment
for violation of professional secrecy
where –
(a) the disclosure of confidential
information is made for the
performance of their professional
duties under this Law;
(b) the disclosure of confidential
information is made to satisfy the
requirements of an agreement
concluded by the NBR with any
other relevant supervisory
authority; or
(c) the disclosure of confidential
information is required by a court
order.
(4) The NBR may provide confidential
information to a public sector entity
and any other agency in accordance
with relevant laws.
69

articles.heading: Exchange of confidential information The NBR may exchange confidential information with a foreign institution having a
articles.text:
similar mission, a foreign bank, a supervisory
authority, a foreign financial regulator or an
international institution, subject to
confidentiality obligations of the receiving
entities.
CHAPTER VI: PROPERTY AND
FINANCE

articles.heading: Financial year, approval and publication of the status of accounts (1) The financial year of the NBR begins
articles.text:
on 01 July of each year and ends on 30
June of the following year.
(2) The NBR approves the status of its
accounts and publishes them in the
Rwanda at the end of each quarter.
(3) The accounts of the NBR are kept in
accordance with international financial
70
reporting standards.

articles.heading: Internal audit (1) The internal audit department of the NBR operates independently to support the NBR in achieving its
articles.text:
strategic objectives, safeguarding its
assets, and enhancing the effectiveness
of its risk management, internal
control, and governance processes.
(2) The internal audit department of the
NBR reports functionally to the Board
of Directors and administratively to the
Management.
(3) The internal audit department of the
NBR adheres to the international
internal audit standards.

articles.heading: Independent audit (1) The independent audit is conducted by an independent auditor appointed by
articles.text:
the Board of Directors.
71
(2) The independent auditor is responsible
for auditing and certifying NBR
accounts of each financial year. The
independent auditor conducts the audit
in compliance with the International
Standards on Auditing.
(3) Each year, the independent auditor
audits the statements including –
(a) the statement of financial position;
(b) the statement of comprehensive
income;
(c) the statement of changes in equity;
and
(d) the statement of income
distribution.
(4) The independent auditor submits the
audit report for the preceding financial
year to the Board of Directors within
the first quarter of the following year.
(5) The term of office of an independent
auditor is one year renewable. Where
an independent auditor has served for
72
an uninterrupted period of five
consecutive years, he or she is not
eligible for reappointment until the
expiry of a period of five years from
the end of his or her last term of office.

articles.heading: Publication of financial statements The NBR publishes in the the Republic of Rwanda the financial
articles.text:
statements, together with the statement of the
use of finances, certified by an independent
auditor, within six months following the close
of the financial year.

articles.heading: Annual activity report Within four months following the close of each financial year, the Governor submits to
articles.text:
the President of the Republic and to both
Chambers of the Parliament, the annual
activity report, including financial statements
for that financial year.

articles.heading: Amortisation of losses (1) The NBR establishes specific accounts for unrealised gains and losses arising
articles.text:
73
from foreign exchange operations and
from fluctuations in the market price of
foreign currencies, gold, financial
instruments and other assets.
(2) Where the annual accounts of the NBR
indicate a loss, the loss is amortised by
charging it against the reserve funds.
Where the balance of the reserve funds
is insufficient to absorb the loss in full,
the NBR applies to the State for
payment of the outstanding amount by
way of recapitalisation.
(3) Within six months of receiving the
request for recapitalisation, the State
transfers to the NBR the required
amount, in cash or in negotiable
interest-bearing securities at financial
market-determined interest rates and
having a fixed maturity date.

articles.heading: Distributable profit (1) The net profit of the NBR is calculated in accordance with International
articles.text:
Financial Reporting Standards.
74
(2) Unrealised gains and losses on foreign
currencies, gold, financial instruments,
and other assets are excluded from the
determination of distributable profit.
(3) From the distributable net profit, 20%
is credited to the reserve funds to
increase the total capital to at least 10%
of the monetary liabilities of the NBR.
(4) After deduction from the net profit of
such other allocations as the Board of
Directors considers appropriate, the
remaining distributable profit is
transferred to the Public Treasury.

articles.heading: Publication of statistical data reports and economic and financial studies (1) The NBR publishes reports containing
articles.text:
statistical data and economic and
financial studies.
(2) The NBR requires a legal entity, public
and private agency, or any other person
to provide it with the statistics and
information needed for the analysis of
75
economic, monetary, credit, balance of
payments and external debt conditions.
(3) Any legal entity or individual
requested by the NBR to provide the
information specified in Paragraph (2)
is bound to provide such information.
(4) The NBR may establish direct
relations with enterprises and
professional groups capable of
providing it with the information
needed for the analysis.
CHAPTER VII: FAULTS AND
ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

articles.heading: Faults and administrative sanctions Regulations determine faults and administrative sanctions imposed on an
articles.text:
individual or legal entity that fails to comply
with its regulations, directives or decisions of
the NBR adopted in the performance of its
responsibilities.
76

articles.heading: Enforcement of regulations, directives and decisions of the NBR The regulations, directives and decisions of
articles.text:
the NBR are binding on all those to whom they
apply. Their application may not be stayed
except by a final decision of a competent court
providing otherwise.
CHAPTER VIII: MISCELLANEOUS
PROVISIONS

articles.heading: Taxes and fees exemption for the NBR
Security of the property of the NBR The State provides free of charge, security and protection of the premises and any other
articles.text:
property of the NBR as well as the necessary
security escorts for the transfer of funds,
securities or any other valuable property.
However, if it considers it necessary, the NBR
77
may have recourse to other security experts.

articles.heading: Term of office of members of the governing organs of the NBR in office at the time of entry into force of this Law
articles.text:
The term of office of the members of the
governing organs of the NBR holding office at
the time of entry into force of this Law is
computed from the date of their respective
appointments.
CHAPTER IX: FINAL PROVISIONS

articles.heading: Saving and repealing provision Except for Article One of Law n° 48/2017 of 23/09/2017 governing the National Bank of
articles.text:
Rwanda as amended, in its provision
establishing the NBR, all other provisions of
that law are repealed.
